title: Explain me how to prove quadratic formula
subtitles:
```webvtt
WEBVTT

00:00.000 --> 00:05.000
Here's how to prove the quadratic formula.
We start with the standard form:

00:05.000 --> 00:09.000
ax squared plus bx plus c equals zero.

00:09.000 --> 00:13.000
First, divide the entire equation by a.

00:13.000 --> 00:17.000
This gives us x squared plus b over a times x plus c over a equals zero.

00:17.000 --> 00:20.000
Next, we complete the square.

00:20.000 --> 00:24.000
First, move the constant term: x squared plus b over a times x equals negative c over a.

00:24.000 --> 00:31.000
Now, add b over 2a, squared, to both sides. This becomes: (x plus b over 2a) all squared equals (b squared minus 4ac) over (4a squared).

00:31.000 --> 00:34.000
Finally, solve for x.

00:34.000 --> 00:37.000
Take the square root of both sides.

00:37.000 --> 00:41.000
This gives us x plus b over 2a equals plus or minus the square root of (b squared minus 4ac) over 2a.

00:41.000 --> 00:43.000
Isolate x.

00:43.000 --> 00:48.000
This gives us x equals negative b over 2a plus or minus the square root of (b squared minus 4ac) over 2a.

00:48.000 --> 00:52.000
Combine the fractions to get the quadratic formula.

00:52.000 --> 00:57.000
x equals negative b plus or minus the square root of b squared minus 4ac, all divided by 2a.

00:57.000 --> 00:59.000

```

title: Show how Goal clashes works
subtitles:
```webvtt
WEBVTT

00:00.000 --> 00:05.000
Welcome to this video on understanding goal clashes.

00:05.000 --> 00:10.000
Goal clashes occur when pursuing one goal actively hinders the achievement of another.

00:10.000 --> 00:11.500
Let's look at some examples.

00:11.500 --> 00:16.500
First, consider the clash between time and quality.

00:16.500 --> 00:22.500
One goal might be to complete a project quickly. The opposing goal is to ensure the highest possible quality.

00:22.500 --> 00:25.500
Speed can compromise quality, and vice versa.

00:25.500 --> 00:30.000
Next, think about cost versus scope.

00:30.000 --> 00:34.500
A goal to minimize project costs can clash with the desire to maximize the number of features included.

00:34.500 --> 00:37.500
Adding features increases cost, while cutting costs limits features.

00:37.500 --> 00:44.000
Finally, let's examine short-term versus long-term goals. Maximizing profit in the current quarter could clash with building sustainable growth for the future.

00:44.000 --> 00:47.000
Short-term gains might sacrifice long-term stability.

00:47.000 --> 00:56.000
When facing goal clashes, identify the conflicting goals, prioritize them strategically based on your overall objectives, and actively seek compromises or alternative solutions that address both.

00:56.000 --> 00:59.000
This video was created by Apilage AI.
```

title: Explain how gravity works
subtitles:
```webvtt
WEBVTT

00:00.000 --> 00:03.000
Let's explore how gravity works.

00:03.000 --> 00:07.500
First, we have Newton's Law of Universal Gravitation.

00:07.500 --> 00:13.500
This law states that the force of gravity is proportional to the product of the masses
and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between them.

00:13.500 --> 00:19.000
The formula is F equals G times m1 times m2 divided by r squared.

00:19.000 --> 00:23.500
Next, we have Einstein's General Relativity.

00:23.500 --> 00:29.000
This theory describes gravity as the curvature of spacetime caused by mass and energy.

00:29.000 --> 00:34.000
Objects follow the curves in spacetime, which we perceive as gravity.

00:34.000 --> 00:40.000
Finally, there are gravitational waves. These are ripples in spacetime
caused by accelerating massive objects, such as black hole mergers.

00:40.000 --> 00:45.000
To summarize, Newton described gravity as a force.

00:45.000 --> 00:50.000
Einstein described it as the curvature of spacetime.

00:50.000 --> 00:53.000
And gravitational waves are ripples in spacetime.

00:53.000 --> 00:56.000
This video was created by Apilage AI.
```
